title: The Lone Ranger Rides Again

evidence.note: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips, 1966 volume, renewal registrations, p. 94: THE LONE RANGER RIDES AGAIN, a series of photoplays by Republic Productions, 2 reels each, claimant Republic Corp. (PWH). Chapters 1-6: registered 25 Feb 1939 as L8730, renewed 1 Jun 1966 as R389272. Chapters 7-11: registered 25 Feb 1939 as L8821, renewed 1 Jun 1966 as R389276. Chapters 12-15: registered 26 Feb 1939 as L8882, renewed 1 Jun 1966 as R389278. All 15 chapters are covered by a 1966 renewal, so the serial is still under US copyright.

editorial:
The Lone Ranger Rides Again is a 15-chapter Republic Pictures serial from 1939. The 1966 Catalog of Copyright Entries (p. 94) shows all 15 chapters registered on 25 and 26 February 1939 and renewed on 1 June 1966. The renewal numbers are R389272 for chapters 1-6, R389276 for chapters 7-11 and R389278 for chapters 12-15. That renewal is why the serial is not in the US public domain.

A creator should therefore not treat circulating copies as free to reuse. Copies on video-sharing sites are not evidence of a lapsed copyright here. The Lone Ranger character and name are a separate franchise-rights question that no copyright expiry would settle, and I did not confirm who owns any active marks. I did not check the music credits, so the score's status is undetermined. To use clips, license them from the rights holder.
faq: Is The Lone Ranger Rides Again (1939) in the public domain in the US?
No. All 15 chapters were registered in February 1939 and renewed on 1 June 1966 (R389272, R389276, R389278), per the 1966 Catalog of Copyright Entries, p. 94.
Can I use clips if the character looks old enough to be free?
No. The renewed copyright covers the serial's footage. The music credits, trademark and story rights in the Lone Ranger character are separate questions, and I did not resolve them.
